native_protocol.description:
Small cell gastrointestinal lymphoma (SCGL) is a type of cancer that affects the digestive tract of cats. It can cause long-term weight loss, vomiting, and diarrhea. The usual treatment for SCGL includes giving pills every day. Some cats do not tolerate these medicines well. This study is testing another treatment option that does not require daily pills. The treatment uses three radiation treatments. The radiation will be given slowly to help protect your cat's digestive tract. Cats may take part in this study if they have SCGL, have had signs of the disease for more than 6 weeks, and have not yet received treatment for SCGL.


We will check your cat after radiation treatment to see how well the treatment works and whether your cat has any side effects. We will also test stool (fecal) samples to learn about the bacteria in your cat's digestive tract.


The goal of this study is to find out if this radiation treatment is safe, well tolerated, and helpful for cats with SCGL. We hope this treatment will improve the quality of life for cats with this cancer.
native_protocol.tagline: Help us learn about the use of radiation treatment in cats with GI lymphoma
native_protocol.name: Radiation Therapy for Small Cell GI Lymphoma in Cats

identity: IACUC 8528. Three consecutive daily fractions totaling 6 Gy to the entire GI tract under anesthesia, with stool sampling and rechecks at 1 week, 1, 3 and 6 months. Named investigator Tiffany Martin, DVM. Distinct from Texas A&M 358215 (different center, eligibility and fractionation), Missouri high-grade GI lymphoma WART+COP/doxorubicin, and Tufts inflammatory-enteropathy RT (excludes GI lymphoma).
recruitment_sites: Official native state Active - Recruiting; individual rendered protocol accepts screening, states recruitment from 2026-11-02. One named site CSU VHEC, 300 W Drake Rd, Fort Collins, Colorado.
eligibility: Feline small-cell GI lymphoma confirmed by endoscopic biopsy. Signs for at least six weeks (overview says more than six; leave exact boundary for coordinator). No previous chemotherapy. Recently changed diet, antibiotics or steroids may be eligible after waiting periods not specified. Adequate condition for anesthesia/radiation. Before enrollment CBC/chemistry, urinalysis, cobalamin/folate, abdominal ultrasound, thoracic radiographs, IHC and PARR within protocol-specific times.
funding: After enrollment the study covers radiation, stool testing and protocol recheck appointments. Owners pay other diagnostic and treatment-related costs; do not infer separate anesthesia or travel coverage.
deadline: Current individual page states recruitment begins 2026-11-02; no end date is published. Six-month follow-up is relative to treatment and not an enrollment cutoff.
